waypoints.name: Ross Dam Trailhead (SR-20 milepost 134)
waypoints.note: US-side approach, opposite the Depot Creek approach used for the West Ridge/Beckey route. Climbers take a water taxi (or boat, portaging Diablo Lake to Ross Lake) up Ross Lake ~15 miles to the Little Beaver landing/dock, then hike/bushwhack up the Perry Creek drainage to reach the base of Southeast Mox Peak's East Face.
waypoints.directions: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east past Newhalem and Diablo to the Ross Dam Trailhead near milepost 134, about 14 miles past Newhalem, and park in the small lot. From here a trail drops about 1 mile through forest toward Ross Dam; at the bottom, turn right on the gravel road to the lakeshore, where a phone on the last power pole calls Ross Lake Resort for the water taxi, which must be reserved in advance.

waypoints.name: Base of East Face Headwall
waypoints.note: Bivy ledge below the 1,500-ft near-vertical headwall of the Devil's Club route.

waypoints.name: Southeast Mox Peak (Hard Mox) summit / East Face high point

itinerary.cal: No fixed anchors exist anywhere on the route — carry a full natural-gear rack for the rappel descent; the wall is typically driest and safest late August to early September.

days.note: Take the Ross Lake water taxi to the Little Beaver dock, then start up the brush-choked Access/Perry Creek drainage toward the base of Southeast Mox. Devil's club and slide alder shred clothing and skin almost immediately — the first-ascent party (Layton & Wolfe, 2005) called this the worst bushwhacking of the whole route.
days.title: Boat taxi + bushwhack into the approach drainage
days.objective: Start the approach toward the East Face

days.note: A second full day of brutal bushwhacking is needed just to reach the base of the 2,500-ft East Face — the FA party spent two full days on approach alone before touching rock.
days.title: Reach the base of the East Face

days.note: About 1,000 ft of steep slabs lead to a small bivy ledge at the base of the near-vertical, 1,500-ft upper headwall. This sets up an early start on the crux the next day.
days.title: Climb the lower slabs to a bivy ledge
days.objective: Reach the bivy ledge below the headwall

days.note: An 18-hour push forces a route through steep, loose, poorly-protected 5.9+ A2- rock to the summit. The descent is a dozen-plus rappels off natural gear anchors (the route has no fixed bolts), reaching the tent around 3:30 AM.
days.title: Summit push and all-night rappel descent

schedule.label: Leave the bivy ledge
schedule.detail: Early start to get a full day on the 1,500-ft headwall above.

schedule.label: Climb the headwall
schedule.detail: Steep, loose, poorly-protected 5.9+ A2- rock — the crux of the route.

schedule.label: Top out
schedule.detail: Reach the summit after roughly 15 hours of continuous climbing.

schedule.label: Begin rappelling
schedule.detail: The first rap anchor hangs up, forcing a strenuous re-climb to free it.

schedule.label: A dozen+ more rappels
schedule.detail: Descend the full face on natural gear anchors — no fixed bolts on route.

schedule.label: Back at the tent
schedule.detail: Return to base camp roughly 18 hours after leaving the bivy ledge.

days.objective: Climb the headwall to the summit and rappel back to camp

days.note: After an all-night push, most parties take a slower recovery day retracing the bushwhack back down the drainage toward Ross Lake.
days.title: Rest and begin the hike out
days.objective: Recover and start descending the drainage

days.note: Finish the brushy descent back to Ross Lake and catch the water taxi back across the lake to the car.
days.title: Bushwhack out and boat back to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A serious 6-day expedition: 2 days of brutal bushwhacking just to reach the wall, 2 days on the 2,500-ft East Face (including an 18-hour summit push and an all-night natural-anchor rappel descent), and 2 more days to recover and hike out.
